text:
Can you write an email to people who didn't renew their farm share? I run a 30-acre vegetable farm and sell 22-week shares that people pick up every Thursday.

Facts:
- Last year 260 households had a share. 97 didn't renew.
- On July 9 a hailstorm destroyed about half our crops. For the next 6 weeks the boxes had about half the usual amount. We didn't offer refunds or credit, and I sent one short email about it.
- A full share is $540 this year, the same as last year.
- This year we've added a second field on higher ground and put up 2 hail nets over our tomatoes and peppers. That cost $31,000.
- Members can now pause up to 2 weeks and get credit for them.
- Sign-up closes March 15. 52 shares are left.

Under 200 words.

I wrote this as a win-back email. The members' complaint about last summer comes first, before you ask them to come back. It's 172 words.

<final_document>
Subject: We let you down last summer

Hi [Name],

You didn't renew your share this year, and I think I know why.

On July 9, a hailstorm destroyed about half our crops. For the next six weeks, your box held about half what it should have. That's roughly three weeks of produce you paid for and didn't get. We didn't offer a refund or credit, and I sent you one short email about it. I'm sorry. You deserved a real explanation and a fair answer, and you got neither.

Here's what we've changed:

- We added a second field on higher ground, so one storm is less likely to hit all our crops at once.
- We put up two hail nets over our tomatoes and peppers.
- You can now pause up to 2 weeks and get credit for them.

All of that cost us $31,000. A full share is still $540, the same as last year.

Sign-up closes March 15, and 52 shares are left. If you'd like yours back, sign up here: [link]

If not, I'd like to hear what would change your mind. Just reply to this email.

[Your name]
[Farm name]
</final_document>

**The email doesn't fix the refund problem.** It apologises for there being no refund or credit, but it doesn't offer anything to make up for it. The six half-boxes came to about $74 of produce ($540 ÷ 22 weeks × 3 weeks). If you could give returning members that amount as a credit, or even a partial one, it would be the strongest thing you could put in this email. If you decide to, add a line after "you got neither," and I'll adjust the wording.
